findings.summary: Gaza medical officials reported that an Israeli strike near a bakery in western Deir al-Balah killed Hussam Nusair and three-year-old Tayyem Hamdan and wounded several others. The Israeli military separately said Nusair was a Hamas operative; that target characterization remains an attributed military claim.
findings.title: Two Palestinians, including a three-year-old child, killed in Deir al-Balah strike
findings.uncertainty_note: The two deaths and additional injuries are corroborated by AP, Reuters, Al Jazeera and WAFA reporting, but the number of wounded is not specified. The military target explanation is separately attributed and not independently established.

findings.title: Two Palestinians killed near Gaza City municipal park
findings.uncertainty_note: Casualty figures come from hospital or medical officials and are corroborated by Anadolu and AP reporting. The military target characterization remains attributed and unsupported by details.

findings.uncertainty_note: The injury and transfer counts are attributed to PRCS through WAFA and corroborated by Anadolu. The precise effect on fishing access beyond the five injured workers is not quantified.

findings.exact_supporting_passage: Water contamination is increasing, acute watery diarrhoea cases nearly doubled, and Gaza's overwhelmed health system is not equipped to manage surges.
findings.historical_review_match_result: No protected historical review matches this measured public-health development.
findings.public_match_result: The Sep. 2 amputee feature is distinct; no public story represents these WHO water and disease measurements.
findings.summary: WHO reported that testing of more than 6,700 water samples showed microbiological contamination rising from under 6 percent in January to over 18 percent in August, while acute watery diarrhea cases nearly doubled from about 27,000 in March to more than 48,000 in August. WHO said Gaza's overwhelmed health system was not equipped to manage resulting surges and lacked access to restricted laboratory and diagnostic supplies.
findings.title: WHO reports tripling water contamination and near-doubling of acute watery diarrhea in Gaza
findings.uncertainty_note: The measurements and capacity assessment are WHO-reported. The WHO remarks do not establish that every diarrhea case was caused by tested water contamination.

findings.summary: WHO said it supported the Aug. 31 medical evacuation of five children from Gaza with 14 companions to Romania and Belgium. Romania's public broadcaster, citing its foreign ministry, reported two children would be treated in Romania and three transferred to Belgium.
findings.title: WHO supports evacuation of five Gaza children to Romania and Belgium
findings.uncertainty_note: WHO directly supports the total and destinations; the two-to-Romania and three-to-Belgium split is separately attributed to Romania's foreign ministry through the public broadcaster.

findings.exact_supporting_passage: PWA reported 55,000 cubic metres of untreated wastewater discharged daily and all five main treatment plants out of operation.
findings.historical_review_match_result: No protected historical review matches this assessment.
findings.public_match_result: No public Gaza story represents this Sep. 2 sewage-system assessment.
findings.summary: The Palestinian Water Authority reported about 55,000 cubic metres of untreated wastewater discharged daily: 40,000 to the sea and 15,000 through cesspits and network leaks. It said all five main treatment plants were out, only 18 of roughly 74 pumping stations were partly operating, sewage-network coverage had fallen from over 85 percent to about 45 percent, and treatment capacity had fallen from about 185,000 cubic metres per day to zero apart from rehabilitation work.
findings.title: Palestinian Water Authority reports Gaza wastewater treatment collapse
findings.uncertainty_note: Every system quantity is attributed to the Palestinian Water Authority through WAFA; no independent engineering audit was identified in the bounded review.

findings.summary: The Palestinian Information Center quoted Gaza Civil Defence official Mohammed Abu Dan saying crews recovered 233 bodies or remains, including 73 children and 106 women, from 20 destroyed homes during a 51-day recovery campaign, while 174 of 407 believed buried there remained missing. He said equipment shortages constrained the ongoing work.
findings.title: Gaza Civil Defence reports 233 bodies recovered from 20 destroyed homes
findings.uncertainty_note: All counts are attributed to Gaza Civil Defence through the Palestinian Information Center and corroborating regional reports; they were not independently audited in this bounded review.
